subject: TrustedHealth retention & log purge cadence — DPA appendix alignment
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@trustedhealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Marco Silva <marco.silva@cloudops.io>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify retention windows + backup purge exceptions for DPA appendix

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As we finalize the DPA addendum I need two items clarified so our legal and cloud ops teams can sign off:

1) Our minimum retention requirement for audit logs is 24 months, but we have strict rules on backup purges (must not delete backups required for investigations). Can you confirm Redwood's default backup purge cadence and whether you support an "investigation hold" that pauses automated purges for specific accounts for up to 90 days?

2) If we need a log retention exception (e.g., HIPAA investigation), what's the operational workflow to request and confirm the exception? Specifically: SLA for acknowledgement, who approves (security vs. legal), and whether you provide forensic snapshots as evidence of non-deletion.

We're preparing a single appendix to attach to the DPA; if you can share a short summary and preferred wording for the retention paragraph, that would be ideal. Attaching our draft DPA checklist (we'll share the appendix in a follow-up).

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Privacy & Compliance
TrustedHealth

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@trustedhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify retention windows + backup purge exceptions for DPA appendix

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then a proposed paragraph for the appendix below.

Summary:
- Default backup purge cadence: 90 days for hot backups; 365 days for immutable archival snapshots (customer-configurable per contract).
- Investigation hold: yes — we support account-level "investigation holds" that suspend automated purge jobs for a configurable window. Standard hold window is up to 90 days; we can extend with legal approval. Holds are applied within 4 business hours of an approved request.
- Log retention exceptions: request via secure ticket to our Security Operations queue (security@redwood.com) — we acknowledge within 4 business hours and target full operational confirmation within 2 business days. Security owns operational approval; Legal is looped for policy exceptions. Forensic snapshots are available as a time-stamped export (read-only) and are retained outside the normal purge cadence for the hold window.

Proposed appendix language (suggested):
"Redwood Inference will retain audit logs and backups in accordance with the customer's contract and the DPA. By default, Redwood rotates hot backups every 90 days and retains immutable archival snapshots for 365 days. Upon customer request for an "investigation hold", Redwood will suspend automated purge processes for the specified account within 4 business hours of an approved request; holds may be granted for up to 90 days and extended upon mutual agreement and documented legal approval. Forensic snapshots produced during holds will be provided as read-only exports and preserved outside the standard purge schedule for the duration of the hold."

I've attached a draft appendix and the latest backup purge timeline spreadsheet for your team to review. Filing this under the DPA as Appendix B would work from our side.

Looping in Karthik to confirm the implementation details and Markus for any acceptable exceptions at the infra level. Marissa included for customer success coordination.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Trust & Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: TrustedHealth_DPA_Retention_Appendix_v1.pdf, redwood_backup_purge_timeline_v3.xlsx

Laura / Elena —

Quick engineering notes and a proposed operational flow we can include in the appendix to make the process actionable:

Engineering constraints:
- Immutable archival snapshots are stored in a WORM-enabled tier; those snapshots require a formal retention override to delete.
- Investigation holds flip a per-account tag that excludes the account from both continuous and scheduled purge cronjobs. The tag is applied by the Security Operations system and is propagated to all storage regions.

Operational flow (recommended):
1) Customer opens a secure ticket (email-to-ticket) to security@redwood.com with case-id and justification.
2) Security acknowledges in <= 4 business hours and applies a temporary hold flag (up to 72 hours provisional) so no purge occurs while evidence is reviewed.
3) Security + Customer agree on hold duration (standard 90 days). If >90 days, escalate to Legal for documented approval.
4) Security produces a forensic snapshot (SHA256 manifest included) and stores it in a read-only bucket; access is audited and provided via a signed, time-limited link.
5) At hold end, Security confirms retention status to the customer and either renews, ships the snapshot to the customer's control, or resumes purge.

SLA notes: we commit to producing a time-stamped forensic export within 5 business days of a signed request (for exports >100GB timelines may extend; we'll notify).

I'll attach a simple diagram of how the hold propagates and a short checklist for SOC evidence pulls so your cloud ops team can validate the process. Markus — can you confirm the expected window for applying the account-level tag across multi-region storage?

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: engineers_log-exception-flow.drawio

2) For the provisional 72-hour hold window — TrustedHealth asks that the provisional hold be immediately confirmed in writing (ticket reply) with the case id and expected decision deadline.

If you make those two clarifications in the appendix we can route to sign-off. We'll return a redline by end of day with one minor timing tweak (requesting a 6 business-day target for large exports >100GB).
